note:
Serbs often take their pets to cafes, restaurants and shopping malls. You may see a «pet friendly» sign on the door.

Popular breeds: Staffordshire, spitz, husky, retriever, French bulldog.

Words: ку̏ћнӣ љуби́мац - pet, па̏с - dog, ма̏чка - cat.
title: Pets in Belgrade

related.en: white bee, the most distant ancestor

note:
Serbian has separate words for ancestors many generations back: пра̀деда, чукундѐда (great-great-grandfather), наврдеда and so on.

By tradition the list goes up to the 16th generation, where «бе̑лӣ о̀рао» and «бела пчела» stand. The eagle stands for strength and immortality, the bee for a swarm of descendants.

In everyday speech only the first two or three generations are used.
title: Names of ancestors in Serbian

note:
Serbs switch to «ти» quickly, even with strangers, and do not find it rude. There are no patronymics.

Formal address is «госпо̀дине» / «госпођо» / «госпођице» plus the surname in the vocative. If you do not know the surname, «госпо̀дине» alone is enough.

The politest way to start a letter: «По̏штова̄нӣ» / «Поштована».
title: Informal or formal «you» in Serbia

note:
Serbian has words in which «р» is the syllable carrier: кр̑в, смр̏т, цр̑в, вр̏т, вр̏х, кр̏ст, гр̑б, тр̏г, бр̑з, пр̏ст, тр̑н, р̏т.

There is no vowel in them, but «р» forms the syllable, and the stress falls on it.

Examples:
• кр̑в - blood
• цр̑в - worm
• пр̏ст - finger
• вр̏х - top
title: Words without vowels

note:
Basic commands:
• «Седи!» - sit
• «Ста̏ни!» - stand
• «Дођи!» - come here
• «Чекај!» - wait
• «Пу̑стӣ!» - drop it
• «Ти̏хо!» - quiet

What you say to an owner: «Ка̀ка̄в фи̑н па̏с!», «Мушко или женско?». What an owner may warn you: «Плаши се», «Може да уједе».

Chatting with other dog walkers is a normal thing in Serbia.
title: What to say to dogs

note:
Color adjectives in Serbian sometimes behave unexpectedly:
• пла̑ва ко̀са - blond hair (literally «blue hair»)
• цр̑нӣ лу̏к - onion (literally «black onion»)
• бе̑лӣ лу̏к - garlic (literally «white onion»)
• црно вино - red wine (literally «black wine»)
• слатка вода - fresh water (literally «sweet water»)
• кисела вода - sparkling water (literally «sour water»)

These pairs are best learned as set expressions.
title: Colors in names

related.en: coffee brought to a boil three times

note:
Serbs like to joke about themselves:
• српска посла - sloppy work and pulling strings
• ср̏пскӣ ѝна̄т - stubbornness out of spite
• српска кафа - coffee brought to a boil three times
• српска Нова година - January 13-14, by the old calendar

These are self-ironic expressions you often hear in conversation and on social media.
title: «Serbian» as irony

note:
The main difference: ekavian (in Serbia: вре́ме) and ijekavian (in Croatia: вријеме).

Other differences:
• after modal verbs a Serb uses «да + present»: хоћу да радим; a Croat more often takes the infinitive: хоћу радити
• future: радићу (Serbian) and радит ћу (Croatian)
• vocabulary: па̑сош - путовница, аеро̀дром - зрачна лука, хи̏љада - тисућа
title: Serbian and Croatian: the main differences

note:
From the Turks came everyday words: џе̏п, шѐћер, ба́дем, па̀мук, јо̀рган, ка̀пија, то́рба, ча̀рапа, па̏ра, ме̏рмер, ђу̏бре, сѝрће, па̀пуча, ћо̀шак, ха̀јде.

Many of them became basic words and are not felt as loanwords.

Serbs use ха̀јде all the time, for «come on» or «let's».
title: Turkisms in Serbian

note:
The website «Mala biblioteka» announced a contest for the best Serbian replacements for foreign words. The winner was «духоклонуће» instead of «депрѐсија», followed by «прохујак» (flashback) and «прикачица» (attachment).

Among the other entries:
• нежељак - spam
• дубоклажа - deepfake
• утицајац - influencer
• промајник - air conditioner

Most of the words are still jokes and have not entered everyday use.
title: A contest for a beautiful new word

note:
The word «ва̀мпӣр» is considered one of the best-known Serbian words in other languages. It spread after the case of Пѐтар Благо́јевић from the village of Кисиљево around 1725: after his death, villagers were said to have started dying suddenly.

An Austrian official described the case in a report, and a fashion for vampires swept across Europe. That is how the word got into many languages.
title: Vampire is a Serbian word

related.en: family feast of the patron saint

note:
Сла̏ва is a family feast in honor of the family's patron saint. It is on the UNESCO intangible heritage list.

How to go to a Slava:
• come to the hosts hungry
• bring a symbolic gift: wine, coffee, sweets or flowers
• say «Срећна слава!» to the hosts

A Slava can be посна (fasting) or мрсна (non-fasting); on the table there is usually жи̏то and a славски колач.
title: How to go to a Slava

note:
The main rule of Serbian spelling: write as you speak and read as it is written.

What it means:
• each letter is always read the same way
• there are no silent letters, as there are in English
• knowing the alphabet lets you read any word at once

Ч and Ћ are different sounds: Ч is hard, Ћ is soft.
title: Write as you speak

note:
In Serbia a death is traditionally announced through читуље: obituary notices in newspapers, on poles and at building entrances.

They give the name, the dates of life, a photo and condolences (са̀учешће) from relatives. One person often gets several чѝтуља from different loved ones, so their number is sometimes taken as a measure of influence.

That is how acquaintances learn about a death and come to pay their respects.
title: Obituaries in Serbia

related.en: to wait for a long time

note:
Montenegrin became official after the 2007 Constitution. Its alphabet has two more letters than the Serbian one: ś and ź (in Cyrillic «с́» and «з́»).

The pronunciation is ijekavian; in Serbia it is ekavian.

In the coastal towns Italianisms are noticeable:
• пја̏т - plate
• ленцун - bed sheet
• ду̀рати - to last

Old words:
• че̏ља̄д - people
• ба̀нути - to turn up suddenly
• дре̏ждати - to wait, long and in vain
title: The Montenegrin language

related.en: Serbian bogeywoman, sister of Baba Yaga
beauty of the mountains and waters

note:
Serbian fairy-tale and mythical beings:
• Баба Рога - the Serbian sister of Baba Yaga: an old woman with a horn who frightens children
• Ба̏ш Чѐлик - a villain like Koschei: his death is hidden in a bird or an animal
• Ала - a demon that swallows the sun and moon during an eclipse; people scared it away with noise
• Ви́ла - a beauty of the mountains and waters
• Мо̏ра - a nightmare spirit that chokes sleepers
• Некрштеници - restless souls of unborn and unbaptized children
title: Serbian fairy-tale and mythical beings

related.en: to tap eggs against each other

note:
Easter in Serbia is celebrated for three days.

Egg customs:
• eggs are dyed (фарбати јаја) with onion skins (ко̏ра од лу́ка)
• the very first egg is red; it is called чува̀ркућа and stays in the house until next Easter; red stands for life
• people crack eggs against each other (куцати се јајима): whoever's egg does not break wins and takes the other egg
• guests bring one egg for each member of the host's household
title: How Serbs celebrate Easter

related.sr: Го̏ре го̏ре го̏ре го̏ре, не̏г' што̏ до̏ле го̏ре го̏ре.
related.en: Up there the forests burn worse than down here.

note:
A word game: «Горе горе горе горе, нег' што доле горе горе».

Words that sound the same:
• го̏ре - up, above
• го̏ре - worse
• го̏ре - (they) burn
• го̏ре - forests (pl. of гора)

The phrase means: up there the forests burn worse than down below. It shows how many homonyms Serbian has.
title: Homonyms: «горе горе горе горе»

note:
February 15 is Serbia's Дан државности. It is tied to two events:
• 1804 - in the village of Orašac it was decided to start the First Serbian Uprising (у̀станак)
• 1835 - on the feast of Сретење the first constitution was adopted in Kragujevac (Сретењски устав)

So the holiday is also a Constitution Day (у̏ста̄в).
title: Statehood Day

note:
Ex-YU rock is the rock music (ро̏к) that developed in the former Yugoslavia (бивша Југославија).

In the 1970s and 80s the scene was vibrant, and musicians from Serbia, Croatia and Bosnia shared fans.

Legendary bands (гру̏па):
• Бијело дугме
• Азра
• Елѐктричнӣ орга̀зам
• Рибља чорба
• Идоли

The songs live on after the breakup of the country.
title: Rock of the former Yugoslavia

note:
To show affection for things and people, a suffix is added to the word:
• feminine nouns more often take -ица: ку̏ћа - ку̏ћица, ма̏чка - ма̏чкица
• masculine nouns take -ић: гра̑д - градић

But Serbian uses diminutives less than you might expect: instead of «little eyebrows, little nails» people just say о̏брве, но̏кти.
title: Diminutive suffixes

note:
Men's costume: a шајка̀ча, a white shirt, a dark пр̀слук, wide trousers, ча̀рапе and leather о̀па̄нци with straps.

Women wore long embroidered shirts and a vest called тлек; belts were an important part.

Patterns can be floral, geometric or charms against evil. In Vojvodina the embroidery is richer, in the south the clothing is simpler. Today the costume is worn on holidays.
title: Serbian folk costume

note:
In Serbia films and cartoons are shown in the original language with Serbian subtitles (тѝтл, pl. титлови), not dubbed.

That makes it easy to practice listening and reading at once, both at the cinema and at home.
title: Cinema in Serbia - with subtitles

pure false-friend article for Russian speakers

note:
In Serbia eggs are dyed on Вѐликӣ пе́так (Good Friday).

The first egg is red and is called чува̀ркућа: it is kept at home, and people believe it protects the house and the family all year.

On Easter Day people play куцање јајима: everyone takes an egg and taps it against an opponent's egg. The one whose egg stays whole wins.
title: Easter eggs: чуваркућа and куцање

note:
Titles and character names of cartoons in Serbia often differ from the English ones:
• Donald Duck - Паја Патак
• Bugs Bunny - Душко Дугоушко
• Smurfs - Штрумпфови
• Minions - Малци
• «Lady and the Tramp» - Маза и Луња
• «Cinderella» - Пепѐљуга
• «The Ugly Duckling» - Ру̑жно па̏че

Learn the terms along with familiar stories: they stick better that way.
title: Cartoon characters' names in Serbian

related.en: in Serbia a layered pie, in Bosnia only with meat

note:
In Serbia бу̀рек is a layered pie, and «бурек са сиром» is perfectly normal.

In Bosnia «бурек» means only the one with meat. Other pies are called differently:
• with cheese - си́рница
• with potatoes - кромпируша
• with spinach - зељаница
• general name - пи̏та

So in Bosnia ordering «бурек са сиром» will cause surprise.
title: Burek: with meat or with cheese

note:
The Serbian ћирилица has 30 letters, and each stands for one sound. The principle of writing: «write as you speak, read as it is written».

Separate sounds got their own letters: «ј», «љ», «њ», «ћ», «ђ», «џ».

That is why there are no silent letters in it.
title: Serbian Cyrillic: 30 letters

related.en: family feast of the patron saint

note:
Serbs jokingly call January све̑тӣ ја̏нуа̄р: one holiday follows another.

• Christmas (Бо̀жић)
• Све̑тӣ Сте̏фа̄н
• the Serbian New Year (by the Julian calendar)
• the сла̏ва of Saint Sava at the end of the month

People work reluctantly at this time and switch to «супер полако» mode.
title: «Holy January»

related.en: wife of one's husband's brother; wives of two brothers

note:
Serbian has many precise words for relatives, which can seem unnecessary to an English speaker:
• uncles - стри̑ц (father's brother) and у̏ја̄к (mother's brother)
• aunt - те̏тка, one word for both the father's and the mother's sister
• uncles' wives - стри̑на and у̏јна
• wives of two brothers - јетрве
• husband's sister - за̏ова

A separate topic is ку́мство: godparents and ку̏мови are considered close family, and such ties are highly valued in the village.
title: Family relationships among Serbs

note:
The end piece of a loaf has different names in Serbia, depending on the region:
• окра̏јак
• крајка
• пупушка - in Vojvodina
• попак, рубак, ка̀нтӯн - in some other places

There is a joking belief about this piece: whoever likes it will get a good mother-in-law.
title: What the end piece of a loaf is called

related.en: I'm living at an easy pace.
tavern, place for food and drink

note:
Пола́ко is not only «slowly». It also means «take it easy, don't take it to heart».

The word has become almost a motto of Serbian unhurriedness:
• an answer to Ка̏ко си? - «I'm living easy»
• attitude to time: па̑р го̏дина can mean four to six years
• attitude to money: small change is not counted, and friends treat each other in the кафана
title: Полако as a way of life

note:
If you write Serbian in the Latin alphabet without š, č, ć, ž, đ, the meaning can change:
• šiške (bangs) and siske are different words
• šišanje (haircut) and sisanje (sucking)
• kuća (house) turns into kuca (little dog, bitch)

So it is better to use the diacritics or to write in Cyrillic.
title: Why diacritics matter

related.en: name of a village or mountain
name of a village or mountain
name of a village or mountain
name of a village or mountain

note:
Serbia has villages and mountains whose names make people smile:
• Мокре Гаће
• Смрључ
• Прљуша
• Курило
• Орал

Locals are not bothered by them, and for tourists they become a reason for a photo by the road sign.
title: Unusual place names in Serbia

note:
Besides the usual ја̏нуа̄р, фе̏бруа̄р and so on, there are folk month names based on natural signs:
• сечањ - January
• вѐљача - February
• тра̑вањ - April
• цветањ - May
• ср̑пањ - July or August
• гро̏здобер - grape harvest time
• ли̏стопа̄д - autumn

The names differ by region and are almost never heard in speech.
title: Old names of the months

related.en: to drink Šumadija tea - to go for a rakija

note:
Шумадијски чај is not tea but a hot drink made from шљивовица or another rakija with sugar, water and, if you like, honey. It is drunk in winter in company, to warm up.

If you hear пити шумадијски чај, you are being invited for a rakija, not for herbal tea.
title: Šumadija tea

note:
Useful questions for the seller:
• Да ли је аутомо̀бӣл по̀лован и̏ли но̏в?
• Колика је километража?

• Када је рађен технички преглед?
• Можете ли показати сервисну књижицу?
title: Phrases for buying a car

related.en: What are you doing, you silly donkey?

note:
Serbian often insults people with animal names:
• ма̀гарац - a fool or a stubborn person
• сви́ња - a slob or a miser
• кра̏ва - a slow person
• змѝја - a treacherous person
• о́вца - someone who blindly follows the crowd

It usually sounds grumbling and playful: Шта радиш, магарче један?
title: Animals in Serbian insults

note:
Serbian has phrases that read the same from left to right and from right to left:
• Ана воли Милована
• Сир има мирис
• Ања себе сања
• Маче једе јечам
• Они воле вело вино

The word «палиндром» is hardly found in textbooks, but this is good practice for reading and vocabulary.
title: Serbian palindromes

note:
New Year: је̏лка, ку́гла, паху̀љица, ва̏троме̄т, Де̏да Мра̏з.

Christmas: Бо̀жић, Бадње вече, а̑нђео, све́ћа, вѐнчић.

Greetings:
• Срећна Нова година!
• Сре̏ћан Бо̀жић!
• at Christmas - Христос се роди! and in reply Ваистину се роди!
title: New Year and Christmas vocabulary

note:
Шопска салата is a salad of tomatoes (пара̀дајз), cucumbers (кра̏ставац), sweet peppers and onions with white brined cheese (си̏р) and oil.

The Shopi are an ethnic group at the meeting point of Serbia, Bulgaria and North Macedonia. The salad has become a symbol of the Balkans, and the name took hold in tourist restaurants in Bulgaria in the 1950s.
title: Shopska salad

note:
Serbian Бо̀жић falls on January 7, by the Julian calendar.

On Christmas Eve (Бадњи дан) a ба̏дња̄к - an oak branch - is brought into the house and burned in the stove.

At the Christmas lunch the family shares the чесница, a round bread with a coin. Whoever gets the coin will have good luck all year.

People greet each other like this: Христос се роди! - Ваистину се роди!
title: Christmas in Serbia

related.en: coffee in the morning to wake up
coffee for a long chat with friends

note:
Serbs have jokey names for coffee depending on the occasion:
• раздремуша - in the morning, to wake up
• дочекуша - for a long-awaited guest
• разговоруша - for a long chat with friends

The words are formed on the pattern «action + -уша». The humor is colloquial and not for the dictionary.
title: Jokey names for coffee

note:
How to dictate an address:
• @ - ет; in conversation there is also ма̀јмунче («little monkey»), but it is not used in business speech
• dot - та̏чка
• hyphen - цр̏тица
• underscore - доња црта

First you specify: све малим словима («all in lowercase»).

Example: ма̑рко доња црта де̏вет јѐдан ет џи мејл та̏чка ком
title: How to dictate an e-mail address

note:
Serbian wedding vocabulary:
• запро̀сити дѐво̄јку - to propose
• вѐридба - engagement
• мла̑да and младо̀жења - bride and groom
• младѐнци - newlyweds
• венча̀ница - wedding dress
• ве̏о - veil
• по́зӣвница - invitation

Guests usually arrive late - all in the spirit of пола́ко.
title: Wedding vocabulary

note:
On social media Serbs often write in the Latin alphabet without č, ć, š, ž, đ, and the meaning changes:
• sisati - to suck, šišati - to cut hair
• sarma - stuffed cabbage rolls, šarm - charm
• kuca - little dog, kuća - house
• kolac - stake, kolač - cake
• strasno - passionately, strašno - terrible

Look at the context.
title: Latin script without diacritics: сисање or шишање?

note:
The Shopi are a group living at the meeting point of Serbia, Bulgaria and North Macedonia, hence the name.

The modern salad was invented in the 1950s for tourists in Bulgaria. It has tomatoes (пара̀дајз), cucumbers (кра̏ставац), pepper, onion, white cheese (бе̑лӣ си̏р) and oil.

Today шопска салата is a dish that symbolizes the whole Balkans.
title: Where Shopska salad comes from

note:
Some Serbs subconsciously believe in the power of words and avoid the dangerous name.

A snake is called непоменица (better not to mention it) or она отровна.

A cancer diagnosis is called најгора болест or она болест.
title: Words people avoid saying directly

note:
In ads for houses for sale it pays to read between the lines:
• прилика за улагање - often a house to be demolished
• топли дом - a run-down building with a stove
• аутентична кућа - an old house untouched by renovation
• потребна мања адаптација - something more serious than cosmetic work
• легализација у току - a building that is not officially registered
title: The language of Serbian real estate ads

related.en: рога, a variety of flat red pepper
капија, a variety of red pepper

note:
Real Serbian а̀јва̄р is made from roasted red peppers of the рога or ка̀пија varieties: flat, fleshy, dark red.

How it is made:
1. Roast the peppers over a fire or in the oven.
2. Steam them under a lid.
3. Peel and grind them.
4. Cook them down for a long time in oil.

The Macedonian version adds патлѝџа̄н (eggplant), and a mix with hot pepper and garlic is called љутѐница.

It is better not to call the pepper «Bulgarian» in front of a Serb.
title: What counts as real ajvar

note:
Кра̏ставац (cucumber) and кра̀стача (toad) come from кра̏ста - a crust, a scab. Both the cucumber and the toad are covered with bumpy skin.

Do not mix up the words: жа̏ба is a frog, and a toad is кра̀стача.
title: The cucumber and the toad are relatives

note:
Some Serbian words are used only in the plural but are feminine. Many of them name one object made of two parts:
• ма̀казе - scissors
• пантало́не - trousers
• фа̀рмерке - jeans
• но̀вине - newspaper
• сао̀нице - sled
• бо̀гиње - smallpox
• жму̏рке - blind man's buff

The rare бука̀гије (shackles) and чезе (a light carriage) are the same.
title: Feminine words used only in the plural

note:
The suffix -џија came from Turkish and denotes a person's trade or inclination:
• ћевабџија - a seller of ćevapi
• шешѝрџија - a hatter
• ча̀мџија - a boatman
• кују̀нџија - an obsolete word, today people say зла̀та̄р

The words галамџија (loudmouth), ларамџија (troublemaker) and силѐџија (hooligan) are formed the same way.
title: The Turkish suffix -џија

to fool someone, to play a prank on someone
literally: a pumpkin without a root

note:
In Serbian the pumpkin is called ти̏ква or бу̀ндева. There are also regional variants: бу̏ча, вр̏г (bottle gourd), лудаја, мисирача, дулек.

Many idioms:
• покондирена тиква
• пукла тиква
• дувати у исту тикву
• садити тикве с неким
